author: miami courant
title: Rep. María Elvira Salazar announces passport event and calls for release of Cuban teen
text:
Rep. María Elvira Salazar, U.S. Representative for Florida’s 27th congressional district, posted a series of updates on her social media accounts regarding federal services in her district and the imprisonment of a Cuban teenager.
On March 23, 2026, Salazar informed constituents about an upcoming event to facilitate passport applications. She wrote, ” Need a passport? Apply before summer travel. On Thursday, April 9th, we’re bringing federal services directly to #FL27. Passport acceptance facilities will be on site to help you apply, and my team will be there to assist every step of the way, no appointments, no hassle.” The same day, she shared a similar message in Spanish: ” ¿Necesitas un pasaporte? Solicítalo antes de viajar este verano. Este jueves 9 de abril, llevaremos servicios federales directamente a #FL27. Habrá oficinas de aceptación de pasaportes en el lugar para ayudarte con tu solicitud, y mi equipo estará disponible para asistirte”.
On March 24, 2026, Salazar highlighted the case of Jonathan Muir Burgos in Cuba: “Jonathan Muir Burgos is a 16-year-old imprisoned by the Cuban regime after protesting. His only “crime” was raising his voice. This is the face of the regime’s brutality: cruelty, repression, and the imprisonment of a child. He must be freed immediately.”
Salazar has frequently used her platform to connect residents with government resources and advocate for human rights issues related to Cuba. As an elected official representing Miami-Dade County—a region with a significant Cuban-American population—she has prioritized both constituent services and international advocacy.
